title: Escalation Request
description: An implementer's request to the director for more reasoning effort or a stronger model, issued instead of a third guess-based fix. The implementer does not change its own model or effort; it stops and submits this request. See ESCALATION-PROTOCOL.md.

request_type.description: EFFORT_ESCALATION: same model needs a higher reasoning tier. MODEL_ESCALATION: a stronger model is needed. An implementer may believe both apply; it may propose both, but must pick the request_type it judges primary.

task.description: The task_id or a short description of the task this request concerns.

root_cause_key.description: A short stable identifier for the suspected root cause, used to check whether attempt_1 and attempt_2 actually targeted the same cause.

failed_test.description: The specific test command or name that keeps failing, if applicable.

attempt_1.description: What the first fix actually changed.

attempt_1_result.description: The observed outcome of attempt_1, in evidence terms (test output, error), not a summary judgment.

attempt_2.description: What the second fix actually changed. Must be a genuinely different approach from attempt_1, not a restatement.

attempt_2_result.description: The observed outcome of attempt_2, in evidence terms.

confirmed_facts.description: What is actually known, backed by evidence — not assumptions.

unresolved_points.description: What remains uncertain or unexplained after both attempts.

model_ceiling.description: The worker model ceiling before any user-approved policy exception.

recommended_model.description: Model names are environment aliases; this is a recommendation, not a directive. The director decides.

regression_risk.description: Risk that a third blind attempt would widen breakage or touch shared contracts.

protected_files.description: Files that must not be touched by a next attempt without explicit director authorization (e.g. shared contracts, security-sensitive paths).

last_passing_test.description: The last known-good checkpoint (test run, commit, or state) to fall back to if escalation does not resolve the issue.

exact_next_prompt.description: The precise instruction the implementer believes should be run next, once escalation is granted — not a vague 'try again'.
